question: According to the 6th Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey conducted by the Labour Bureau, which age group had the highest participation in the labour force in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**25-29**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 6th Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey conducted by the Labour Bureau, the age group **25-29 years** had the highest participation in the labour force in India.
 
• This survey highlights labour force participation trends across various age groups, aiming to understand India's workforce dynamics.
 
• The **labour force participation rate (LFPR)** measures the proportion of the working-age population actively engaged in the labour market, either employed or seeking employment.
 
• The **25-29 age group** represents individuals often transitioning into stable employment after completing education and gaining initial work experience.
 
• These trends are critical for policymakers to address employment generation strategies and skill development initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**

 
 
• LFPR is a key economic indicator representing the percentage of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• In India, LFPR has historically been lower compared to global averages, particularly for women.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate:**
 
 
• The unemployment rate indicates the percentage of the labour force that is without work but actively seeking employment.
 
• It is a crucial metric for assessing the health of the economy and the effectiveness of employment policies.
 
 
 
• **6th Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey:**
 
 
• Conducted by India's Labour Bureau, this survey provides insights into employment trends and labour force dynamics.
 
• It categorizes data across sectors, age groups, gender, and regions to assist in informed policymaking.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development Initiatives:**
 
 
• Government schemes like **Skill India** aim to enhance employability by providing vocational training and skill development.
 
• Such initiatives help bridge the gap between workforce needs and available skills in the labour market.
